text:
alex: Heads-up — saw a 10-15% GPU memory spike when moving a TP job from TP=2 -> TP=4 on the 80GB nodes. Not just model shard growth, NCCL staging/async-copy buffers appear to be much larger. Anyone else see this?

marta: Yep, I observed the same in last night's perf sweep. NSYS trace shows lots of cudaMemcpyAsync + cuBLAS workspace allocations between shards. My hunch is allocator fragmentation + per-stream transient buffers.

jon: Dropped a quick nsys capture here: https://ci.example.com/artifacts/1918765432/nstats.nsys
Key snippet from the flame summary: 
```
cudaMemcpyAsync  ·  12k calls  ·  28MB peak staging
cuBLASLtGetMatrix  ·  4k calls  ·  transient workspace grabs
cudaMalloc       ·  fallback allocations on contention
```

kevin: That matches an allocator pathology we talked about. Current default uses a single global arena with a mutex. With more TP streams we see lock contention, which pushes paths to call cudaMalloc (small allocations) and causes fragmentation. Two immediate mitigations: per-stream arenas (lock-free fast path) + fixed-size comm-staging ring reused across iterations.

alex: I prototyped an allocator patch that preallocates a comm staging pool sized to max_comm_bytes_per_rank * nranks and recycles bufs round-robin. Quick bench on 8x A100: peak dropped from ~62GB -> ~56GB, OOMs vanished. Patch snippet: 
```cpp
// simplified pseudo
pool.reserve(max_comm_bytes);
void* get_staging(size_t s) { return pool.next_fit(s); }
void release_staging(void* p) { /* noop, ring buffer */ }
```

marta: Nice improvement. Another wrinkle: cuBLAS/cuBLASLt will ask for per-stream workspaces on first use and those stay reserved. We should either set a global workspace cap (cublasLtSetAlgoAttrs or driver flag) or reserve a per-layer workspace from the allocator to avoid unexpected cudaMallocs.

jon: Quick before/after from the canary run (perf-bot):
BEFORE: peak=62.1GB, avg=58.3GB, OOMs=3, throughput=480 tokens/s
AFTER:  peak=56.4GB, avg=53.9GB, OOMs=0, throughput=479 tokens/s  :thumbsup:
So latency/throughput didn't regress, memory headroom improved.

kevin: Two follow-ups: 1) add unit/integration test that stresses allocator reuse across concurrent streams (simulate many small async copies). 2) run a fragmentation sweep across TP sizes {1,2,4,8} and collect allocator heatmaps (we have hooks to emit alloc/free histograms).

alex: On it. Also noticed KV-cache shadow copies: when prefix-kv spills to CPU and we do NCCL AllGather for cross-shard cache placement, we sometimes create ephemeral host/device staging copies per shard. That duplicates RAM for a short window. I'll dedupe the spill->gather path so the CPU buffer is shared rather than copied per-ranked op. Filing an issue.

sandeep: FWIW batching heuristics interact here too. The new micro-batching change created many more small requests which increases kernel launch rate and transient alloc churn, exacerbating fragmentation. Dropping min-batch wait by 1ms reduced churn noticeably in my experiments.

perf-bot: CI job 1918765432-alloc-pool-per-stream finished. Artifacts: https://ci.example.com/results/1918765432. Quick summary: peak mem -9.2%, OOMs -100%, P99 latency +0.1%.

jon: Action items:
- alex: finish pool + add tests + land canary. (owner: alex)
- marta: add cublas workspace cap and test stability. (owner: marta)
- kevin: run fragmentation sweep across TP sizes and post histograms. (owner: kevin)
- sandeep: measure batching heuristic delta and propose throttle if needed. (owner: sandeep)
- perf-bot: run nightly regression with the pool enabled on 4x/8x configs.

alex: I'll open the PR and ping eng-runtime for review. tagging @eng-runtime.

marta: Sounds good — small step wins, then iterate on workspace + KV dedupe.

kevin: Great work. Let's keep the allocator change behind a flag for now so we can A/B safely.

jon: If anyone hits weird perf cliffs, drop NSYS captures + allocator histograms on the issue.

alex: Will do. Thanks all. :rocket:
